data.why: The app bundles three demo protein sequences in code and its own example top-down MS/MS mzML file; the same mzML is copied to data/ so the browser agent can also exercise the 'Upload mzML' file-uploader path, not just the 'Load example mzML' button.

goals: Load a demo proteoform (e.g. Human Insulin B chain) and view its annotated sequence coverage map with matched c/z fragment ions
Switch ion types (c/z vs b/y) and charge states to see how fragment coverage and matched-ion counts change
Load the bundled example top-down mzML spectrum (or upload one) and inspect real MS2 peaks against theoretical fragments
Compare an experimental spectrum to theoretical fragment ions in the Mirror Plot, adjusting mass tolerance (ppm) and reading per-peak Δppm error
Export the matched/annotated fragment ion table as CSV for downstream reporting

review.summary: The tree is a well-evidenced, replayed account of what actually works in ProteoClinView: setup, tuning the match, the mirror-plot comparison, the error table and export. Every screen I sampled matches its node. It needs fixes before filing because the app's headline goal, the residue-to-peak coverage map, is broken and appears only as a footnote, and several unreachable components and the reason settings don't carry over are missing or misdiagnosed.
